candidate_matrix_revisions.effect: The originally planned signal_card event-mode approach was replaced with a direct D-frequency screen_lane calendar-rule batch, because signal_card's excess return is relative-to-market-average and a same-day, all-stocks calendar event (every stock gets the same pre-holiday signal on the same day) cancels out in that relative framing -- it cannot answer 'does holding pay off'.

sources.core_claim: Extending Ariel (1990) to 1983-2019, the pre-holiday premium now exists only among small firms; the large-firm premium has essentially disappeared, especially after 1990 (VW t-stat falls from 7.03 to 1.92, DJIA/S&P 500 1983-2019 t-stats 0.64/0.93 insignificant; EW-VW pre-holiday difference 0.07pp, t=2.32).
sources.project_applicability: Primary source for this iteration's small-cap-vs-large-cap ETF split, the pre-holiday day definition, and the pre-registered low-Sharpe magnitude expectation.
sources.reflection: Index/decile-level, not ETF-level -- no direct test of IWM/IJR/IWC/VB/SPY/QQQ. Cost/decay risk: ~9-10 trades/year and a per-session premium of only 0.14-0.37pp means costs (10-20bp per side) could plausibly consume a large fraction of the gross premium; this is reported explicitly in report.md, not assumed away.
